# testkit

## Maturity

**Grade:** 2 · S2 E1 A2 H1 P2 · limited by scope (parity), audit (src it ran over not recorded), performance (within 1.1× of the reference, not at it) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — Zig 0.17 `std.testing` (extended), against proptest/Hypothesis (shrinking), insta (goldens), criterion and `testing.B` (bench skeleton) for the pieces this module carries; strategies, snapshot update and bench statistics are documented gaps (Backlog) (surveyed 2026-10-17)

**Audit:** review 2026-09-04 · mutation 2026-10-17 (25/26, 1 eq) · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-17 (TESTKIT_FUZZ, clean: hex 2M, golden 1M, fault 1.6M, tape 240k runs; 5 planted mutants all killed) · ct n/a — test helpers (keyword review, 2026-10-07)

**Performance:** ref 1.03–1.07× a bare seed loop over the same harness · fastest ref (measured 2026-10-20)

**Evidence:** model-fuzz — `hex` against a from-scratch nibble decoder, golden `diff`/`render`/verdicts against a naive first-difference scan and a string-built rendering, the fault transports against their input, the choice tape against the PRNG it records (`src/fuzz_test.zig`); hex also against a strict RFC 4648 decoder over all 16276 short inputs (tools)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

The harness pieces every module's tests were re-deriving. **Test-only**: it is
wired into each consumer's test binary through `build.zig`'s `test_deps`, never
into the module a downstream user imports — `@import("frost")` does not drag a
test harness along with it.

- **Status:** complete. **Platform:** any.
- **Deps:** none (std only).
- **Model after:** `std.testing`, extended with the helpers this repo's own
  tests kept re-deriving.

## Compared with

This module is a deliberately small, test-only harness ("everything in this module was measurably duplicated first"), so the yardstick is what a Zig test author already has (`std.testing`) plus, for each piece it carries, the tool a user would otherwise reach for: proptest/Hypothesis/rapid for shrinking, insta for goldens, criterion and `testing.B`+benchstat for the bench skeleton. Claims come from READMEs and Zig 0.16.0's `lib/std/testing.zig`, else *(inferred)*. No foreign source was read. Coverage-guided fuzzing engines (libFuzzer, AFL++) are a different class — exploration, not a seed-loop verdict — and are not compared.

**Where we are ahead:** a fuzz *verdict* in seconds rather than exploration (`std.testing.fuzz`/`Smith` explores and reports no progress or reach): per-input watchdog with `HANG seed=N`, seed file and replay of a saved input, reach counters, and a choice source that does not degenerate to range minimums. A failing seed is then **shrunk** on a recorded tape of draws (block deletes, zeroing, binary-search lowering, whole-slice cuts), every candidate in a forked child, accepted when the outcome class is the same (error / signal / leak / hang), and ends in a traced replay of every draw plus an in-process `<PREFIX>_CHOICES=<file>` replay. The Zig ecosystem rows above are property libraries with typed generators, and none is shown (from READMEs) to do process-isolated outcome-matching shrinking, but this is *(inferred)*. Fault injection is drawn from the same source (chunked `Reader`/`Writer` with failure at a drawn byte, `FailingAllocator` with a drawn index), plus guard-page buffers. `testkit.bench` provides the comparison skeleton, with alternating rounds ours/ref/alt in one run and cycle-based ratios, which std lacks. The golden failure names the first differing offset and a bracketed window and reports length mismatch separately. `check-testonly` proves the harness cannot leak into a published module. **Where we are behind:** no strategy/combinator library (proptest, rapid, Hypothesis, minish and zcheck have one; here shrinking works on raw draws, so the reported minimal case is a tape, not a typed value), no snapshot-update (insta/ohsnap-style review/accept) workflow, no structural diff beyond byte slices, no statistical analysis in `bench` (criterion, benchstat: confidence intervals, significance), no stateful/model-based testing (rapid) and no coverage-guided exploration (libFuzzer/AFL++/`Smith`-based fuzz). Backlog: the first two are what the Zig ecosystem rows cover.

## What is here, and why only this

Everything in this module was **measurably** duplicated first. It is not a
place to put things a test might one day want.

| Piece | Was duplicated |
|---|---|
| `verboseSkip` / `skip` | 42 byte-identical copies across 26 modules |
| `hex.bytes` | 18 byte-identical copies across 8 modules |
| `expectHex` / `expectBytes` | every `goldens.zig` spelled it differently |
| `loopbackSkip` | the hand-written "loopback bind failed, skipping" give-up in ~25 modules (2026-10-01) |
| `fuzz.driver.run` / `fuzz.Rng` / `fuzz.driver.hit` | the deterministic fuzz driver, copied by hand into seglog and zstd (2026-09-27) before qap needed it a third time |
| `stackprobe.Probe` | the dead-stack probe engine, copied into 55 modules' `stackprobe_test.zig` (27.8k lines, 2026-10-09) with hand-derived needles for every intermediate secret; this one needs none — residue below the burn is found without needles, and only secret inputs/`out` buffers are needles |
| `bench` | the comparison driver behind the `**Performance:**` line: 18 crypto-style `tools/bench.zig` carried the same ~200 lines (`Cycles`, `timeIt`, `foreign`, `drive`, …) and 20 Go-stdlib benches a ~80-line `timeIt`/`goBuild`/`goRun` (2026-10-17) |
| `guard.Guarded` | brotli's input-at-a-PROT_NONE-page buffer (2026-10-15), the instrument the guard-page fuzz rule (CML) asks every `[*]`-reading decoder for |

Three pieces are here because the evidence asked for them rather than because they were copied: **shrinking** (every fuzz FAIL was diagnosed by hand from a whole random input), the **fault transports and allocator** (mqtt 2026-10-17: a double free visible only with a transport that fails halfway), and the shrinker's forked-child runner.

The golden comparison is the one piece that is *better* than what it replaced,
not merely shared — see below.

Deliberately **not** here: netns setup and privileged-capability probing. Those
read genuinely differently per module (`tc` wants a fresh netns with `lo` at
ifindex 1; `ebpf` wants `CAP_BPF` in the *initial* user namespace, where
`unshare -r` actively lies to you), and a shared abstraction would hide exactly
the distinctions that make those skips correct. The VOPR side is already a
module: [`netsim`](../netsim).

## Use

```zig
const testkit = @import("testkit");

// Skips. Returns the error, so `return` cannot fall through to the
// assertions it was meant to skip.
if (!haveCapability()) return testkit.skip("needs CAP_BPF (uid {d})", .{uid});

// A test that cannot get a loopback socket. A skip anywhere else; a FAILURE
// under scripts/lib/netns-run (ZIGLIBS_NETNS=1), where loopback is guaranteed
// and a skip would be a green run that did nothing.
const listener = addr.listen(io, .{}) catch |err|
    return testkit.loopbackSkip("loopback listen failed ({t})", .{err});

// Hex, in the three shapes the repo uses.
const key = comptime testkit.hex.bytes(32, "000102...");   // KAT vectors
const got = try testkit.hex.into(&buf, wire_hex);           // caller buffer
const owned = try testkit.hex.alloc(gpa, wire_hex);         // allocated

// Goldens.
try testkit.expectHex("45000054...", frame);
try testkit.expectBytes(expected, actual);
```

## The deterministic fuzz driver

`zig build --fuzz` explores; it cannot give a verdict (no progress, exit 0 on a
crash, a hang is invisible). `fuzz.driver.run` runs the same harness over
inputs drawn from seeds, in the ordinary ReleaseSafe test binary, with a
watchdog per input:

```zig
fn harness(comptime S: type, src: *S, gpa: std.mem.Allocator) anyerror!void {
    var buf: [512]u8 = undefined;
    const n = src.slice(&buf);
    if (n > 100) testkit.fuzz.driver.hit("long input");   // reach, printed at the end
    try parse(gpa, buf[0..n]);
}
test "fuzz: the parser" {                       // exploration, optional
    try std.testing.fuzz({}, struct {
        fn f(_: void, s: *std.testing.Smith) !void { return harness(std.testing.Smith, s, std.testing.allocator); }
    }.f, .{});
}
test "fuzz driver: the parser" {                // the verdict
    try testkit.fuzz.driver.run(harness, .{ .prefix = "MOD_FUZZ", .name = "parser" });
}
```

`MOD_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` runs it (unset: skipped; a harness with `.scale = N` runs `runs / N`, so one budget suits a parser and a whole protocol exchange), `MOD_FUZZ_ONLY`
selects harnesses by name, `MOD_FUZZ_MS` is the limit per input (2000),
`MOD_FUZZ_SEEDFILE` holds the current harness and seed for a crash,
`MOD_FUZZ_INPUT` replays a saved `--fuzz` input. Output: `runs …` about once a
second, `DONE <name> runs=… in … ms`, `REACH <name> <label>=<n>`, and
`FAIL <name> seed=N: <error>` / `HANG <name> seed=N` (exit 124). One job per
core with disjoint seed ranges is the caller's runner. The source of choices
is `fuzz.Rng` — never `Smith{ .in = random bytes }`, which answers the range
minimum for almost every draw. The driver runs on 64-bit Linux
(`fuzz.driver.supported`) and skips everywhere else without compiling its
Linux code, so a module that uses it can still declare 32-bit or Windows
targets.

## Shrinking a failing seed

`FAIL`/`HANG` lines are followed by the command that shrinks them:

```
FAIL testkit-golden seed=2: TestExpectedEqual
  smallest input: TESTKIT_FUZZ_SHRINK=2 TESTKIT_FUZZ_ONLY=testkit-golden
```

`<PREFIX>_SHRINK=<seed>` reruns that seed with its choices recorded on a
**tape** (one `u64` per draw: a ranged draw's offset from its minimum, a
length, a byte, an enum's position), then tries smaller tapes — whole slices
cut (length and bytes together), blocks deleted, blocks zeroed, single
entries lowered by binary search — each in a forked child, keeping one when
it ends **the same way** (the same error, the same signal, a leak, a hang).
A panicking or hanging candidate costs a child, not the shrink. The result
is printed as a traced replay:

```
SHRUNK testkit-golden seed=2: 168 -> 6 choices (336 candidates)
choices: 2 1 1 4 2 1
  #0 slice[2] = 0101
  #1 fuzz_test.Mutation = .scatter
  #2 range 0..6 = 2
  #3 index <2 = 1
  ...
```

`_SHRINK_OUT=<path>` writes the tape (one number per line), `_CHOICES=<path>`
replays it in-process with every draw printed (for a debugger), `_SHRINK_MS`
is the budget (60 s). Recording lives inside `fuzz.Rng` (an optional `tape`),
not in a second source type, because 93 modules' harnesses branch on
`S == Rng` — a different type would record a different input than the one
that failed. The approach is Hypothesis's choice-sequence shrinking; no code
of it is used. In the shrinker's children core dumps are off and the debug
info is loaded once before the first fork: crashing candidates cost 0.07 s
for this module's panic test instead of 4.5 s.

## Faults drawn like any other choice

```zig
const plan = testkit.fuzz.FaultPlan.draw(src, input.len);
var r = testkit.fuzz.ChunkedReader.init(input, plan, &rbuf);   // short reads, ReadFailed at a byte
var w = testkit.fuzz.ChunkedWriter.init(&out, plan, &wbuf);    // short writes, WriteFailed at a byte
var fa = testkit.fuzz.failingAllocator(src, gpa, 32);          // half the time, fail from allocation k on
```

`Reader.fixed` and `Writer.Allocating` test the one transport that never
happens — everything at once, never an error. These put where the stream
breaks and where it fails into the input, so the driver explores them, a
seed replays them and the shrinker reduces them (one-byte chunks and a fault
at byte 0 are the small end). Only `valueRangeAtMost`/`value` are drawn, so
the harness also runs under `std.testing.Smith`.

## Guard pages

`testkit.guard.Guarded(cap).tail(len)` is `len` bytes ending at an
unreadable page, `head(len)` `len` bytes starting after one: a read past the
end (or before the start) faults under the seed that made it. A differential
fuzz cannot see such a read when every implementation compared shares the
code doing it, and a `[*]` read has no bounds check even in ReleaseSafe
(brotli 2026-10-15). One region per type, mapped once; a plain buffer off Linux.

## The comparison bench driver

`testkit.bench` is what a `tools/bench.zig` times with: `timeIt` (batch
doubled past 100 ms, best of five, user-mode cycles when the counter opens),
`foreign` (`<exe> <dir> <workload>` printing `name ns cycles count`, or
`name ns count`), `drive` (per workload the sides alternate for `rounds`,
ratios ours/ref and ours/min(ref, alt), spread over 5 % flagged, a differing
output count fails the run), `goBuild`, `buildForeign`, `foreignOnce`.
`Work(Op)` carries the three variations the copies had grown: `info` (shown,
not in the verdict), `ours_foreign` (our side timed by the foreign program),
`wall_only` (a threaded op). The scoring (`score`, `Summary.add`) is pure and
is what the tests check.

Its own measurement, `zig build bench-testkit`, found the driver's seed file
costing ~9 µs per seed (`ftruncate` + `pwrite`; a 0.3 µs harness ran 30×
slower, and every runner sets the seed file) — invisible to a cycles ratio,
since it is kernel time. It is now a shared mapping of the file with the
digits incremented in place, and the watchdog reads no clock per input.

## The golden diff

`std.testing.expectEqualSlices` prints both slices in full. For the goldens
this repo actually has — a 200-byte netlink datagram from `iproute2`, a GOOSE
frame, a DER certificate — that is two walls of hex and you still have to find
the difference by eye. `expectBytes` names the first differing **offset** and
shows a window around it with the offending byte bracketed:

```
golden differs at offset 44 (0x2c): expected 0x08, got 0x0c
  offset 36..
  expected:  00  00  01  00  00  00  00  00 [08] 00  01  00 ...
  actual:    00  00  01  00  00  00  00  00 [0c] 00  01  00 ...
```

A golden failure is nearly always "one field moved", and the offset names the
field. A **length** mismatch is reported separately and first: a truncated
encode is a different bug from a wrong byte, and conflating them costs a
debugging cycle.

The comparison (`diff`) and the formatting (`render`) are pure functions and
are what the tests exercise. That is not tidiness — a test asserting "this
comparison fails" would otherwise print its own diagnostic on every green run,
and this repo treats any stderr from the suite as a real problem.

## ⚠ The one thing not verified here

`verbose_skip_env`'s **value** — the string `"ZIG_LIBS_VERBOSE_SKIP"` — is not
pinned by any test, and cannot be: a test reading the same literal it checks is
circular, and a test binary cannot set a variable for itself. A typo would
silently mean "never verbose" forever. The decision *logic* is tested
(`verboseEnabled`); the name is held only by `scripts/test.sh` and the docs
using the same spelling. Grep before renaming.

## Verify

```
zig build test-testkit                          # Debug
zig build test-testkit -Doptimize=ReleaseFast   # ReleaseFast
zig build check-testonly                        # the isolation claim
zig build bench-testkit                         # the driver's cost per input
TESTKIT_FUZZ=200000 zig build test-testkit -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe   # the fuzz verdict
```

`check-testonly` is the one worth knowing about. `test_deps` claims the
published module never needs the harness, and **nothing checked that**: Zig
analyses container-level decls lazily, so an unused `@import("testkit")` in a
module's non-test code is simply never looked at. Verified by planting
`pub const leaked_probe = testkit.verbose_skip_env;` in `netlink` — every
dependent still built green. The step forces the analysis with a
consumer-shaped probe, and the planted leak then fails it while
`zig build test-netlink` stays green.

Forcing that analysis also compiles public code nothing had ever referenced,
which immediately found two dead-but-broken declarations: `enip`'s
`UdpDiscovery.send` constructed an `Ip6Address` with fields Zig 0.16 does not
have, and `ethtool`'s `max_error_message` took `.len` of a *type*.

Provenance: original work of the zig-libs authors (MIT); a thin layer over
`std.testing`. No third-party source consulted or copied, so no `NOTICE` entry
is required (root [`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE) §0). DATA: none. `src/golden.zig` is named for what it compares, not for what it holds — it is a diffing helper with no vendored bytes at all, and this module ships no test data, no fixture and no corpus of any kind. (The catalog gate's data-file check matches on the filename and so names this file; the answer is that there is nothing there.)

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** in-process test-utility layer over std.testing, no wire/crypto

**Reference-class check anyway:** `modules/testkit/tools/README.md` — even a class-C decision benefits from a second opinion; `hex.into`/`.alloc` match a from-scratch strict RFC 4648 decoder on all 16 276 exhaustive short inputs (0 diffs), and disagree with Python's own `bytes.fromhex` only on its whitespace leniency (255/16 276, all in the stricter direction).

## Performance

**Re-measured on Zig 0.17.0, 2026-10-20** (`zig build bench-testkit`, `BENCH_ROUNDS=5`, wall time, largest spread 3.7 %): driver/bare 1.03 (`hex`), 1.04 (`hex+seedfile`), 1.07 (`alloc`, `alloc+seedfile`). The first 0.17 run read **4.24×** on `hex`: the 0.17 migration gave every seed its own `SafeAllocator`, whose init + deinit (`threads: [128]Thread`) cost ~1 µs, against a 0.3 µs harness. The driver now renews it per batch (1024 seeds or 64 MiB allocated) and pins a leak on its seed through a counting `SeedLedger`. The bare loop now also allocates through one `SafeAllocator` (it used the `DebugAllocator` directly, which on 0.17 cost 25 µs a seed for two allocations, so the `alloc` rows read 0.03× — not a comparison).

## Backlog / deferred

- ~~Shrinking for `fuzz.driver`~~ — done 2026-10-17 (see "Shrinking a failing seed").
- **Model-based op-sequence harness** (`ops` vs a model, generic over Impl/Model; proptest-state-machine, Go `rapid`): E1 waves 10-11..10-17 wrote a `model_test.zig` per module, in shapes that differ. Count the shared part before adopting (this module's admission rule).
- **Mutant switch** (`testkit.mutant("id")` over one env var, for schemata runs): every mutation run re-writes the switch; the runners themselves stay disposable (CONVENTIONS §9). Admit once two runs would have used it.
- **Statistics in `bench`** (survey 2026-10-17: criterion, benchstat): `drive` reports best-of-rounds and a spread warning, no confidence interval or significance test. The A/B rule (`feedback_ab_standalone_harness`, CML) covers sub-10 % decisions today; admit when a card decision needs it.
- **Multiplexed cycle counter not detected** (2026-10-21, found by tlsserver's bench): `Cycles.read` reads the raw count; when the PMU multiplexes (other perf users, the NMI watchdog, more events than counters) the count covers only part of the run and the best-of-rounds picks the undercount — a ratio by cycles then disagrees with wall time. Ideal: open with `PERF_FORMAT_TOTAL_TIME_ENABLED | _RUNNING` and treat `running < enabled` as no counter (wall time), on both sides (the C harness is copied per module, so the shared C block needs the same). The leak of one counter per `drive` call that triggered it is fixed (`Cycles.close`).
- **Shrinking a `std.testing.Smith` input** (`_INPUT`): the tape covers the driver's `Rng` only; a `--fuzz` crash input is replayed whole.
- **Golden-update mode (`ZIG_LIBS_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites the expected literal)** (survey 2026-09-30): insta's review workflow; goldens here are hand-edited hex. Effort medium (source-literal rewriting in Zig is awkward; a sidecar-file variant is easier). Fits §2. Verified absent: `rg -i 'shrink|snapshot|update|minimi' src/` finds nothing.
- **Deliberately not doing (existing reason)**: netns and capability probing helpers stay out (see "Deliberately **not** here" above: they read differently per module).
